question.question: Does the VerifyLeader support tally exclude a configured nonvoter acknowledgment from the voter quorum used to confirm current leadership?
question.importance: A false authority confirmation could undermine the API use of preventing stale FSM reads after leadership loss. The local counting discrepancy alone does not establish a stale read.
contexts: One active leader tenure and one verification request
event_paths: VerifyLeader -> verifyCh -> verifyLeader -> peer notify maps -> heartbeat/replication completion -> notifyAll -> verifyFuture.vote -> leaderLoop result

supporting_behavior_ids.b-membership: Suffrage defines participants and threshold; replication includes nonvoters.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-leader-context: Lease and tenure cleanup independently limit stale authority.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-append: Actual follower response producer accepts a current-term heartbeat without voter-specific response filtering.

counterevidence: Lease checks explicitly count only voters and can independently terminate leadership.
A positive nonvoter response can accurately report that it recognizes the sender; it does not alone demonstrate another leader exists.
Commitment and elections already filter voter eligibility; this question is scoped to verification support.
unknowns: Actual post-registration tally and completion when the only additional positive acknowledgment comes from a configured nonvoter.
A legal producer-to-consumer schedule distinguishing nonvoter support from pending voter callbacks.
question.trigger_rationale: Developer documentation identifies voters as the verification support participants; quorumSize computes their majority. Registration and notification instead cover all replication peers. A bounded local eligibility comparison can observe whether a nonvoter acknowledgment increments that count; it need not infer a global stale read or wait for a numeric progress deadline.

obligation.description: Within a stable configuration and an active leader verification request, an acknowledgment from a configured Nonvoter must not increase the support count toward the voter quorum used by VerifyLeader to confirm leadership.

scope.description: Participant eligibility in the per-request VerifyLeader quorum tally, with an unchanged mixed voter/nonvoter configuration and no concurrent leadership/configuration transition during the measured accounting step.
assumptions: Correct peer identities and suffrage; non-Byzantine, well-formed acknowledgments.
An active verification request with initial self support and a configured voter-majority threshold.
excluded: Whether another leader is actually elected.
Membership changes during verification, transport impersonation and restart recovery.
A guarantee that a permitted voter acknowledgment necessarily completes verification.

grounding.derivation: src-verify-doc describes verification by heartbeats to voters; src-verify-contract identifies confirmation of leadership as its purpose, including prevention of stale reads. src-config-types distinguishes Voter and Nonvoter roles. The actual threshold is quorumSize, whose src-lease definition counts voters only. Therefore the support count being compared against that threshold must count eligible voters: an arbitrary nonvoter cannot substitute for one of those participants. The code that registers all replication peers and counts notifyAll results is the subject of comparison, not normative authority that weakens this requirement. The requirement is necessary eligibility accounting, not an assertion that a quorum always succeeds or that every excess tally causes an observed stale read.
grounding.applicability: Stable mixed-suffrage configuration, locally active leader verification, response identity known independently of its success value.
alternatives: Independent voter-only lease checking can later demote a leader, but does not change the participant eligibility of this verification tally.
Sending heartbeat messages to nonvoters is not itself forbidden; counting their acknowledgment toward a voter quorum is the checked distinction.

rationale: Ground the selected local participant-eligibility obligation using implementation-specific developer documentation and API purpose. Formal execution will separately establish whether nonvoter acknowledgments affect the count.

feedback.answered: The verification responsibility is grounded locally: docs/README.md names voters as the confirmation participants, while quorumSize computes a voter majority. Existing verification tests cover all-voter success, a single voter, rejection after term change, and partial connectivity; none of the read cases supplies a mixed-suffrage eligibility witness. A nonvoter may recognize the leader but cannot provide one of the voter contributions required by this tally.
